case_name: B.S. Mathur and Another v Union of India and Others
facts: These writ petitions, u/art. 32 of the Constitution of India, are filed by the directly recruited Additional District and Sessions Judges who were appointed to the Delhi Higher Judicial Service praying for an order quashing the Resolution dated 18.05.2007 of the Full Court of the High Court of Delhi approving the majority report of the Administrative Committee determining the seniority of the petitioners in terms of O.M. dated 03.07.1986 and also quashing the final seniority list of the officers of Delhi Higher Judicial Service.
All the candidates who applied were screened and ultimately 90 candidates were called for interview which was conducted from 16.9.1994 to 20.9.1994.
The DHJS was constituted in the year 1970 under Delhi Higher Judicial Service Rules, 1970 hereinafter referred to as 'the Rules'.
Rule 5 provides for the method of recruitment by way of promotion from amongst the officers of the Delhi Judicial Service and Direct Recruitment.
As originally framed, Rule 16 provides for creation of temporary posts in the service and filling up of the same only by way of promotion from amongst the Members of the Delhi Judicial Service.
The seniority of DHJS officers was not settled by the High Court of Delhi ever since the year 1992.
Till 1980, only substantive appointees to the service from the Bar as also promotees were being given seniority under Rule 82..
In 1980, a writ petition was filed in this Court by the promotee officers challenging Rules 7 and 8 of the Rules, which provided Rota and Quota.
The High Court had also decided that in order to restore the balance between the number of direct recruit appointees and promotees, 14 existing vacancies are to be filled up by direct recruitment.
Consequent to the said direction, the Rules were amended by Notification issued on 17.3.1987.

In the meanwhile, certain promotees and direct recruits of DHJS have filed Writ Petition No. 490 of 1987, Writ Petition No. 1252 of 1990 and others before this Court raising issue as to whether inter-se seniority between the promotees and the direct recruits had actually been determined as per directions given by this Court in O.P. Singla's case.

Pursuant to the said decision, the officers of DHJS appointed/promoted to the service against vacancies prior to the amendment of the Rules, 1987 have given seniority on the basis of the principle of length of service.

In these writ petitions, the claim of the petitioners was that 14 temporary posts which were in existence in 1986 should have been filled up by promotion from amongst the Delhi Judicial Service Officers as per the Rules then existing.
issues: Whether the Resolution dated 18.05.2007 of the Full Court of the High Court of Delhi approving the majority report of the Administrative Committee determining the seniority of the petitioners in terms of O.M. dated 03.07.1986 is valid?
Whether the final seniority list of the officers of Delhi Higher Judicial Service should be quashed?
Whether the inter-se seniority between the promotees and the direct recruits has actually been determined as per directions given by this Court in O.P. Singla's case?
petitioner_arguments: The petitioners argued that the Resolution dated 18.05.2007 of the Full Court of the High Court of Delhi approving the majority report of the Administrative Committee determining the seniority of the petitioners in terms of O.M. dated 03.07.1986 is invalid.
They also prayed for appropriate direction to respondent Nos. 1-4 to determine the seniority of the petitioners in terms of Rule 82. read with Rule 7 of the Delhi Higher Judicial Service Rules, 1970.
respondent_arguments: The respondents argued that the Resolution dated 18.05.2007 of the Full Court of the High Court of Delhi approving the majority report of the Administrative Committee determining the seniority of the petitioners in terms of O.M. dated 03.07.1986 is valid.
They also contended that the final seniority list of the officers of Delhi Higher Judicial Service should not be quashed.
court_reasoning: The Court held that the Resolution dated 18.05.2007 of the Full Court of the High Court of Delhi approving the majority report of the Administrative Committee determining the seniority of the petitioners in terms of O.M. dated 03.07.1986 is invalid.

It also quashed the final seniority list of the officers of Delhi Higher Judicial Service and held that their inter se seniority must be re- determined on the basis of continuous length of service in the cadre, as indicated in O.P. Singla's case.
holding: The Court ordered that the Resolution dated 18.05.2007 of the Full Court of the High Court of Delhi approving the majority report of the Administrative Committee determining the seniority of the petitioners in terms of O.M. dated 03.07.1986 be quashed.

It also directed that the inter se seniority between the promotees and the direct recruits be re- determined on the basis of continuous length of service in the cadre, as indicated in O.P. Singla's case.
